question.text: Mr. Vivek Saxena, a high-income resident LP, receives pass-through LTCG of INR 5 crore on unlisted shares from Krishna Private Equity Fund (Cat II). Mr. Saxena's total income puts him in the peak surcharge bracket (which would otherwise be 37%). Under the post-Budget 2022 rules, what is the surcharge rate applicable on the LTCG component?

answer.text: 15% (capped at 15% for LTCG and certain STCG).

explanation.text: The Logic: From Finance Act 2022 onwards, surcharge on long-term capital gains under Section 112/112A (and on STCG under Section 111A for listed equity) is CAPPED at 15% even where the taxpayer's total income would otherwise attract 25% or 37% surcharge. Hence Mr. Saxena's INR 5 crore LTCG on unlisted shares (taxed at 12.5% base, plus 15% surcharge on that tax, plus 4% cess) benefits from the cap. The peak 37% surcharge only applies to his OTHER income (slab income). The Trap: Option A applies the peak surcharge to LTCG, ignoring the 15% cap. Option B is an intermediate surcharge slab. Option D is too low — the cap is 15%, not 10%. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same 15% surcharge cap. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) tests this heavily because PMS clients are typically in the top surcharge band. X-B (IA L2) uses it for client after-tax planning. Remember: the cap applies to LTCG and STCG under 111A only, not to ordinary income or interest income. Manager's Pro-Tip: When pitching a Cat II PE fund to an UHNI LP, always present the after-tax IRR using the 15% LTCG surcharge cap rather than the 37% peak. Many LPs model conservatively at 37% and under-state your fund's attractiveness — your IR deck should highlight the capped surcharge scenario.
